title: A formally verified hexadecimal digit extraction for pi with an explicit guard for every position (Lean 4 development)
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib development accompanying the paper by Brian Bernard Taylor. Toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0-rc8; Mathlib pinned at 816ff4582a01b10567d1d4ecb10be7c4ff92aab4. Every headline theorem uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; there is no sorry and no native_decide (certificates are checked with decide +kernel).

Proved results:

  • pi equals the Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe series (bbpSeries_eq_pi).
  • Soundness of a guarded natural-number certificate [lo, hi]: whenever lo = hi, the common value is floor(16^n · pi), so its residue mod 16 is the n-th hexadecimal digit of pi.
  • An explicit irrationality-measure bound at the denominators 16^k: |16^k pi − p| · 16^(570k) > 2^−7182802 · 16^k for all integers p and all k ≥ 1.
  • For every position n, every guard depth g ≥ 569n + floor(log16(n+1)) + 1 + 1795710, and in particular every g ≥ 570n + 1795711, returns the correct digit (namespace BBPPi).
  • Kernel-checked facts about runs, distances and the guard depth needed at individual positions.
  • A capped certificate is correct for n ≤ 2000 (checked in CI) and n ≤ 10000 (non-default library BBPHeavyCerts, checked by a local build), and is provably wrong on an explicit window of positions near 2^272. Positions between these ranges are unchecked for the capped certificate.

Build: lake exe cache get && lake build.
